edition: Courses of Study 2026-2027, Computer Science (BS), College of Engineering
pageRules: Computer Science Electives: complete two 4000+ level computer science electives (6 credits). CS 3700 or CS 3780 allowed if not used towards a CS core requirement. CS 4090, CS 4997, CS 4998, CS 4999 are not allowed.
Practicum or Project Course: select one of the listed courses (2-4 credits).

Technical Electives: three 3-credit 3000+ level courses that have a qualifying prerequisite (9 credits). One 2000+ level course is allowed. CS 4090, CS 4997 and CS 4998 are not allowed. Any CS course of 3 or more credits at or above the 3000 level is eligible. Up to two research courses may count.

A technical elective needs at least one qualifying prerequisite or corequisite from the list, as listed in the course's catalog entry for the semester it is taken; a 'recommended' prerequisite is insufficient.

Or by course text: a 'college-level biology' prerequisite or corequisite; second-semester calculus (integration and series, such as MATH 1120 or MATH 1910); or 'probability', 'statistics' or 'introductory statistics'. Courses needing only basic, introductory or differential calculus do not qualify.
Or by chain: a listed prerequisite or corequisite that itself has a qualifying prerequisite or corequisite.

External Specialization: three 3-credit 3000+ level courses in a topic area other than Computer Science (9 credits). They must share a departmental prefix or an advisor-approved topic. At most 1 course cross-listed with CS. Not research, independent study, project team, PE or teaching credit.
Major-approved elective: a single 3+ credit course or courses totalling 3 credits. Letter grade or S/U. No AP/IB credit.
Physical Education, ROTC courses under the 3000 level, and courses under the 1100 level do not count towards the CS degree requirements.
All electives must be at least 3 credits, except the CS project course (at least 2 credits).
